input.question: What makes treeline altitude (highest trees can grow) vary from place to place?
input.ground_truth: Water and heat availability. In general, a you get higher, both become more scarce until it's too cold and dry for any trees to grow. Of course, a mountain in the desert will hit the dryness limit sooner than one in the tropics, and one in Canada will hit the coldness limit sooner than one in Florida.

Question: What makes treeline altitude (highest trees can grow) vary from place to place?

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you have a big box of seeds, and you want to plant them on a big hill. Some seeds can grow really high up on the hill, but after a certain point, the hill is too cold, too windy, or doesn’t have enough soil for the trees to grow. That highest spot where trees can still grow is called the "treeline." 

But every hill or mountain is different! Some hills are warmer, some are closer to the sun, some have more rain or better soil. So, the highest spot where trees can grow (the treeline) is in a different place on every hill or mountain. That’s why the treeline is not always at the same height everywhere.
